summary: CrewSignal is an evidence-based cardiovascular dashboard built for non-doctor astronauts facing 22-minute communication delays. It replaces generic medical thresholds with gravity-adaptive personal baselines to manage microgravity fluid shifts. Featuring "an interactive Body Map," "offline SBAR triage," and "a knowledge graph" tracing every insight to NASA/CSA research, CrewSignal acts as an autonomous digital flight surgeon. An included "Earth Clinic Mode" adapts this exact technology to empower underserved rural healthcare workers.
details:
The Deep-Space Problem

During deep-space transits (eg., to Mars), communication delays of up to 22 minutes prevent real-time Flight Surgeon intervention. Furthermore, in microgravity (0g) and lunar gravity (0.16g), the human cardiovascular system undergoes severe fluid shifts and autonomic remodelling. Current medical dashboards rely on generic Earth-normal thresholds, which trigger false alarms in space, leaving non-doctor astronauts without actionable context.

How CrewSignal Works (System Architecture)

CrewSignal solves this by replacing generic thresholds with gravity-adaptive personal baselines.

The system operates across three core layers:

  • Capture (Computer Vision & Manual): Astronauts can log vitals manually or use our lightweight, browser-based Computer Vision module. By pointing a camera at a standard blood-pressure monitor, the system runs local OCR to extract Systolic, Diastolic, and Heart Rate data instantly, reducing manyal entry errors during emergencies.
  • Analyze (Derived Hemodynamics): The backend (Python/FastAPI) calculates derived metrics critical to aerospace medicine, including Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP), Pulse Pressure, and Shock Index, comparing them against the astronaut's preflight SQLite baseline.
  • Act (SBAR Handoff): Instead of prescribing medical treatment, the system outputs non-diagnostic triage stabilization steps and packages the data into a standard SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) telemetry packet for Mission Control.

The Astronaut User Experience (UI/UX)

Because astronauts operate under high cognitive load, we engineered a single-viewport, zero-scroll "Bento Box" interface.

  • Clinical Anatomical Body Map: We replaced standard charts with a translucent, medical-glass human silhouette. This provides spatial, visual alerts (e.g., baroreceptor shifts) using aerospace-grade targeting reticles.
  • Picture-in-Picture(Pi) Guidance: To ensure usability without thick manuals, every module features a toggleable PiP window explaining exactly How, Where, and For What to use the function.
  • 3-Minute Orthostatic Timer: A built-in protocol timer guides astronauts through the exact supine-to-stand procedure required to test orthostatic intolerance.

Scientific Validity & Super Intelligence (SI)

To eliminate the risk of SI "hallucinations," we built a Neuro-Symbolic architecture.

Every baseline deviation, multi-indicator pattern and triae recommendation is routed through our NetworkX knowledge graph. This means the SI Co-Pilot can only generate insights that explicitly trace back to our verified baseline literature: the NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Hazard/Risks and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) radiation guidelines. CrewSignal operated as a TRL 3 proof-of-concept and clearly labels all data as synthetic and non-diagnostic.

Terrestrial Impact: From Mars to Myanmar

The ultimate impact of CrewSignal extends for beyond the spacecraft.

By toggling "Earth Clinic Mode," the exact same offline baselline-tracking engine and CV OCR scanner translates microgravity fluid-shift protocols into terrestrial clinical tools. This allows community health workers in remote, underserved rural clinics only only in Myanmar but also all around the world to accurately monitor post-bed-rest dehydration, elderly fall risks and orthostatic hypotension without needing an on-site specialist or continous internet access.

Development Tech Stack

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Tesseract.js.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, SQLite, NetworkX, NumPy, SciPy.
